q: A 3x3x3 cube is painted red, then cut into 27 small cubes. How many small cubes have NO red face on them?
a: 1 -- only the cube buried in the very centre of the big cube.

q: A clock takes 5 seconds to strike 6. How long does it take to strike 12?
a: 11 seconds. There are 5 gaps between 6 strikes (1s each) and 11 gaps between 12 strikes -- the strikes themselves are instant.

q: A man walks 1km south, 1km east, 1km north -- and ends up back where he started. Where on Earth is he?
a: The North Pole. (There are also infinitely many starting points near the South Pole that work, but the Pole is the clean answer.)
312211. Each term describes the previous one out loud: 1 is 'one 1' = 11; 11 is 'two 1s' = 21; 21 is 'one 2, one 1' = 1211; and so on.

q: OTTFFSSE -- what letter comes next, and why?
a: N. They are the first letters of One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Six, Seven, Eight -- so Nine.

q: How many squares (of ANY size) are on a chessboard?
a: 204. Sum of squares: 1x1 has 64 positions, 2x2 has 49, 3x3 has 36, ... 8x8 has 1. 64+49+36+25+16+9+4+1 = 204.

q: A bat and ball cost $1.10 together. The bat costs $1 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?
a: 5 cents. (Most people guess 10c, but then bat+ball = $1.20.) Solve: ball = $0.05, bat = $1.05, total = $1.10.

q: What is the smallest positive number divisible by every digit from 1 to 9?
a: 2520. It must be divisible by 8 (so divisible by 2 and 4 too) and by 9 (so by 3 too). LCM(1..9) = 2520.
